To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Gli1 is required for cellular accumulation of cisplat in a cisplatin-resistant cell line, and that the mechanism for this is through inhibition of cellular efflux of drug.

Gli1 contributes to the cellular accumulation of cis-platin in cis-platin-resistant A278O-CP70 cells; that this effect is due to altered cellular accumulation of cisplat-in; that this effect on accumulation is mediated, in part, through inhibition of the cisplatin effux transporter; and that this effect is mediated by a mechanism that is not related to the known effect of Gli1 on nucleotide excision DNA repair.

Gli1 is a key factor in the cellular accumulation of cis-platin; that this is accomplished through the regulation of cellular efflux of the drug, and not by regulation of cellular uptake of drug; and, that Gli1 may play a role in protecting DNA from lethal DNA damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a molecular mechanism by which a transcription factor regulates cellular accumulation of cis-diamminedichloroplatinum (II), a widely-used anticancer drug, in cisplatinum-resistant ovarian cancer cells.
the identification of molecular targets for therapeutic intervention in the cellular resistance to cis-platin and other anticancer compounds.
the role of GBS-binding transcription factors in the cellular accumulation of cis-platin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the role of Glib1 in the cellular resistance of cisplatin-resistant cells is through altered cellular accumulation and altered efflux of cisplatint through the combined action of multiple cisplatin trans-membrane transporters.
the Gli1 transcription factor is a critical factor for the cellular accumulation of cis-platin in cisplatin resistant ovarian cancer cells.
Gli1 contributes to cisplatin resistance by regulating cisplatin accumulation, through regulation of the cellular expression of cisplatin transporters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cellular DNA damage is a strong regulator of Gli1, and that Gli1, in turn, plays a strong role on cellular DNA repair, and on cellular accumulation of cisplatins.
Gli1 is a master regulator of cisplatin resistance.
the Gli1 transcription factor plays a significant role in cellular resistance to cis-platin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Gli1 may be a target for the development of new anticancer agents, that will be effective against platinum-resistant cancer cells.
Gli1 is a key regulator of cellular accumulation of cisplatins, and that it may be a key regulator of cisplatin resistance in human cancers.
the cellular accumulation of cis-platin, and its subsequent efflux, is under the control of Gli1, and that this is a major contributor to the cellular resistance of these cells to cisplatin.
